enquiry: Our dairy process includes a relatively clear whey stream before a concentration stage. We want to investigate whether spectroscopy can track protein concentration as the stream changes, with laboratory results used as the reference. The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions. We need a first measurement concept that handles this change rather than assuming the liquid always remains clear.

intake.summary: Dairy producer asks whether in-line spectroscopy can track protein concentration in a relatively clear whey stream before a concentration stage, where the stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions, with laboratory results as reference. They want a first measurement concept that handles the clarity change.

recommendations.rationale: Whey is named in the dairy literature as a typical stream for NIR transmission, and NIR suits remote fiber-probe measurement in-line. The pathlength must be controlled, and the turbid states must be tested rather than assumed away.

recommendations.rationale: NIR diffuse reflection is the dairy geometry for opaque or concentrated products, so it is the natural fallback when the whey turns turbid. Its sensitivity to surface characteristics and particle size means the turbidity change itself must be characterised.
recommendations.conditions: Applies when the stream becomes too turbid for transmission; reflection signals must be checked for sensitivity to surface and particle effects.

assessment.chemometrics_note: A PLS calibration for protein will need reference samples spanning both the clear and turbid operating states, and scatter correction (e.g. MSC or SNV) is likely needed for reflection data, as in the dairy example on S01 p.17.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The goal is continuous in-line tracking of protein as the stream changes; NIR diode-array instruments allow fast whole-spectrum acquisition suited to monitoring, per S01 p.10.
assessment.future_direction: If the trial shows one geometry cannot cover both states, a dual-technique NIR probe arrangement, or later a combined probe concept, could be evaluated for permanent installation.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the turbidity stays low under all operating conditions, a single transmission/transflection probe (O1) may be enough; if the stream becomes opaque, reflection becomes the primary geometry and the trial design shifts accordingly.
proposal.next_step: Run the multi-geometry NIR trial on representative clear and turbid whey samples with laboratory protein reference results, after agreeing the accuracy criteria.

assessment.brief_answer: Start with an in-line NIR probe trial on the whey stream: transmission or transflection while the stream is clear, plus a diffuse-reflection geometry for the turbid periods, with laboratory protein results as the calibration reference. The key open points are how turbid the stream actually becomes, the protein range and accuracy needed, and the installation constraints; these decide whether one transflection probe suffices or two geometries are needed.

items.finding: In one published spectroscopic process calibration, temperature was deliberately varied, alongside concentration and ionic strength, in order to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests treating temperature variation as a calibration design factor rather than only an auxiliary measurement: the whey calibration could include samples spanning the expected temperature range, and a temperature sensor could still be used to flag conditions outside that range. It gives a reason to test whether temperature variation during turbidity changes affects the whey spectra.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a lithium-recycling liquid-liquid extraction study with a different matrix, chemistry and spectroscopy setup, so the magnitude of temperature effects may differ substantially in whey. It describes model design, not the use or placement of a temperature sensor in-line.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E03 ¶19

items.finding: For a continuous process at a fixed probe location, published guidance is that calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, with validation relying on independent steady-state runs and monitoring focused on drift and out-of-specification detection.
items.how_it_applies: This informs how laboratory results could be used as a reference: validation against independent steady-state runs, with lab values anchoring the calibration within the operational envelope, is a published pattern worth testing for the whey stream. It also implies drift monitoring rather than assuming the calibration remains valid.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement comes from an FT-IR and Raman study in lithium recycling, a different matrix, analyte and spectroscopic method from whey protein NIR. It also assumes a steady-state window, which may not hold when the whey becomes more turbid under some operating conditions.

citation.quote: In contrast, a continuous process at a fixed probe location is intended to operate in a steady-state window, which simplifies the model design: calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, validation can rely on independent steady-state runs, and online monitoring focuses on drift and out-of-specification detection rather than resolving the rapidly changing composition.
citation.label: E03 ¶8
